Questions

What people usually ask before they start using the library.

Yes. Every component is free for personal and commercial projects under the MIT licence, so you can use, change and ship it in client work.
The HTML, CSS and JavaScript for that component. It needs the shared core once, which holds the tokens, icons and small helpers, and you can copy that from the code view, or run npx designme add with the component name and both land in your project.
Yes. Every component has a React version for Next.js, React and Astro: run npx designme add with the component name and --react, and the component lands in your project with its styles. A Tailwind version is in progress on the roadmap.
It's coming. The Figma library is in progress on the roadmap, with every component in Blueprint and Soft, light and dark mode and five accent colours, all built on variables so you can restyle it in one place. Sign up and you'll get it as soon as it lands.
Webflow and Framer exports are coming soon. Until then the HTML version works in a Webflow embed or a Framer code component.
Two visual styles for the same components. Blueprint is technical and square with an orange accent, Soft is rounded with pastel colours, and both work in light and dark mode.
They use proper roles and labels and respect reduced motion, and most work fully with a keyboard. A few, like Kanban and File explorer, are still getting their keyboard support. Test them in your own product too, since accessibility depends on how they are used.
Often. Each release is listed in the changelog, and subscribers get it first.
Yes. Suggest it on the roadmap and upvote the ones you want, and we build the most wanted first.
